steps.body: A triangle's **largest angle** names its family, reusing the acute/right/obtuse vocabulary you already know. **Acute triangle:** every angle under 90°. **Right triangle:** one angle exactly 90°. **Obtuse triangle:** one angle over 90°.

widget.prompt: Sort each triangle's three angles into its family.

widget.missFeedback: Find the LARGEST angle in each triangle, then compare it to 90°.
widget.successFeedback: 60-60-60 and 50-60-70 are acute; 90-45-45 is right; 100-40-40 is obtuse.

predict.reveal: Two right angles already total 180° — the third angle would get 0°, and the sides would run parallel instead of closing. One right angle is the maximum.

steps.body: A triangle can have **at most one** angle of 90° or more. Why? All three angles must add to 180° — if two angles were each 90° or more, they alone would total 180° or beyond, leaving nothing (or less) for the third.

explanationVariants: Two 90°+ angles would already reach 180° or more, leaving zero or less for the third — impossible.
A real triangle can't have two angles that large.

widget.prompt: Could a triangle have two obtuse angles (both over 90°)?

options.label: No triangle can — two such angles would already exceed 180° alone
options.feedback: Two angles over 90° would sum past 180° by themselves, leaving no room for a valid third angle.

options.label: Yes, if the third angle is very small
options.feedback: Even a tiny third angle can't rescue it — two angles over 90° already sum past 180° on their own.

options.label: Yes, in a big enough triangle
options.feedback: Size doesn't matter — every triangle's angles sum to exactly 180°, regardless of how large the triangle is drawn.

options.label: Only equilateral triangles can't do this
options.feedback: Every triangle is bound by the same 180° total, not just equilateral ones — two angles over 90° is impossible for any triangle.

options.label: Right — one angle is exactly 90°
options.feedback: The largest angle, exactly 90°, makes this a right triangle.

options.label: Acute — the other two angles are small

options.label: Can't classify roof trusses this way
options.feedback: The same angle rules apply to any triangle, roof truss or otherwise. This one's largest angle is 90° — right.

takeaways: A triangle's largest angle decides its family: acute, right, or obtuse.
Every triangle can have at most one angle of 90° or more.
The same acute/right/obtuse vocabulary from single angles now classifies whole shapes.
